body:
I suggest renaming the argument to `--rendering-latency` to match the existing `--rendering-method` and `--rendering-driver` arguments. This should reduce the risk of typos when entering the CLI argument name, which can be problematic as Godot doesn't warn when using unknown command line arguments.

```suggestion
	print_help_option("--rendering-latency <mode>", "Override the renderer low latency mode [\"high_framerate\", \"low_latency\"].\n");
```

body:
```suggestion
			- [b]Prefer High Framerate[/b] tells the renderer to prioritize higher framerate by allowing the CPU to queue up additional frames before they're rendered by the GPU. This allows the CPU and GPU to work in tandem, improving the framerate and framepacing in complex scenes at the expense of input latency. This default setting is suitable for most games, especially those that target lower performance hardware.
```

Very simple 3D games that target mobile devices should also use this "prefer high framerate" setting, so I believe something like the suggested text is more suitable for the documentation.

body:
> as the sequential low latency mode prevents the CPU and GPU from running in parallel, which may adversely affect performance by as much as 30-50% under load

I'd rephrase to:

> as the sequential low latency mode prevents the CPU and GPU from running in parallel, which will adversely affect performance by as much as 30-50%. e.g. [b]it's expected[/b] to see a scene that runs at 1000 FPS suddenly runs at 500 FPS in low latency mode, and a scene that used to run at 90 FPS ends up running at 45 FPS.

The reason behind these changes is that:
- It doesn't have to be under load. Halving the framerate can often be expected even under low load conditions.
- **Psychological:** Users _will_ report "CPU\_GPU\_SYNC\_SEQUENTIAL causes a huge reduction in FPS" because they think losing 500 FPS is a lot when it was running at 1000FPS and report this as a bug that needs to be fixed. While we can't stop fools from acting foolish, we can at least try to minimize the amount of false bug reports.

body:
When I say "under load", I mean "the combined sequential time of CPU and GPU processing takes longer than the time between V-Syncs". For a 2D pixel platformer, these times are often very low so with V-Sync enabled, switching to Sequential will have basically no impact on framerate. The reduced framerate happens when the CPU and GPU processing can no longer fit within the same V-Sync interval.

Of course, when you disable V-Sync, said interval becomes zero so in that case you'll see a reduced framerate. And I imagine a lot of users will probably turn off V-Sync to try and measure performance, so I can see how that would be a tech support issue.

I'm open to workshopping the wording here. But I also think it's important to illustrate exactly what scenarios cause the framerate to drop and why.
